findings.evidence: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean:39 `def Modules := SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf` with a separate `Category` instance at :46-48 (`Hom := Modules.Hom`); Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf.lean:90-92 `toSheaf` obj/map; Mathlib/.../SheafCohomology/Basic.lean:125-133 the two naturality statements.
findings.fix: Introduce one bridging functor, e.g. `def Scheme.Modules.toSheafAb (X : Scheme.{u}) : X.Modules ⥤ Sheaf (Opens X).grothendieckTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u} := SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.ringCatSheaf`, with two documented `rfl`-lemmas `@[simp] lemma toSheafAb_obj_obj_obj (M : X.Modules) (U) : ((toSheafAb X).obj M).obj.obj (.op U) = Γ(M, U)` and `@[simp] lemma toSheafAb_map_hom_app (f : M ⟶ N) (U) : ((toSheafAb X).map f).hom.app (.op U) = f.app U`. Define `Cohomology`, `functorH`, `cohomologyZeroEquiv` through it, and prove the naturality lemmas by `simpa using Sheaf.H.equiv₀_naturality isTerminalTop ((toSheafAb X).map f) x`. This also removes the six repetitions of `_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.ringCatSheaf` (lines 60, 64, 71, 107, 116, 125).
findings.issue: `cohomologyZeroEquiv_naturality` and `cohomologyZeroEquiv_symm_naturality` are closed by `by exact CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.equiv₀_naturality ...`, but Mathlib's statement is `f.hom.app (op T) (H.equiv₀ F hT x) = H.equiv₀ G hT (H.map f 0 x)` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean:125-131), while the goal is written with `f.app ⊤` and `((functorH X 0).map f).hom`. The `exact` succeeds only by unfolding `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app φ U = (forget₂ _ _).map (φ.val.app (.op U))` (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean:119), `SheafOfModules.toSheaf` (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf.lean:90-92), `PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf`, and `Functor.comp`. Nothing in the file records that these identifications are the load-bearing step; a restructuring of `toSheaf` or `Hom.app` that preserves all stated Mathlib lemmas breaks all four proofs silently.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Iso.lean:471-475; Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Basic.lean:531-537; Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean:55-59 uses `Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply` as a plain simp/rw lemma.
findings.fix: Replace both proofs with `simp [cohomologyEquivOfIso]` (both `Functor.mapIso_hom` and `Iso.addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply` are already `@[simp]`), or state them as `rfl` with a one-line comment saying which definitional unfolding is used.
findings.issue: `cohomologyEquivOfIso_apply` and `cohomologyEquivOfIso_symm_apply` use `rw [← Functor.mapIso_hom]` followed by `exact ((functorH X i).mapIso e).addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv_apply x`. Both cited lemmas are `@[simps]`-generated `rfl`-lemmas (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Iso.lean:472 `@[simps] def mapIso`; Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Basic.lean:532-537 `@[to_additive (attr := simps!)]`), so this is a `rfl` dressed as a two-step named-lemma chain that additionally leans on delta-unfolding the `def cohomologyEquivOfIso`. The `← rw` direction is the fragile part: it breaks if `Functor.mapIso` is ever restated non-definitionally.

summary: Every declaration in the file typechecks only by delta-unfolding across three wrapper layers (the `Scheme.Modules` type synonym with its own `Category`/`Preadditive` instances, `SheafOfModules.toSheaf`, and `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app`), and the naturality lemmas are closed by bare `exact` of Mathlib lemmas whose statements are syntactically different. Factor the identification into one named bridging functor with explicit `rfl`-lemmas instead of leaving it implicit at six sites.
